note: Order on even days to cover the next 2 days of demand, item 0 ×1.1 and item 1 ×1.15; main risk is shortages on high-demand days, since the plan can't react to actual sales.
Order every day for exactly one day's demand (×1.1 / ×1.15); low storage costs, but the fixed fee is paid 27 times (1512).
3-day cycle with only 9 fixed fees; risk: warehouse overflow plus higher storage costs and shortages, because orders are at about the mean with no buffer.
2-day cycle with a large buffer (×1.2 / ×1.25); fewer shortages, but leftovers build up, item 0 spoils, and units are lost to overflow.
2-day cycle ordering exactly the forecast with no buffer; storage is cheap, but the multiplier averages about 1.046, so shortages and lost high-margin item 1 sales are frequent.
2-day cycle on odd days, with a bridging order on day 0 to cover day 3; demand peaks land in different cycles, but it pays one extra fixed fee.
Asymmetric: item 0 at the forecast so it doesn't spoil, item 1 at ×1.3 to protect its margin of 8 + penalty of 6; risk: item 1 leftovers pile up and cost 0.9 per night.
The opposite asymmetry (item 0 ×1.15, item 1 ×1.05); cheaper storage, but more shortages of the more valuable item 1.
